bug_semantics: perf_group_detach() unlinks a sibling from the leader sibling_list and decrements nr_siblings, but leaves the sibling group_leader pointer at the old leader. That is safe on DETACH_DEAD (sibling about to be freed). It is a use-after-free when the sibling is detached and kept alive, as on CPU hot-unplug DETACH_GROUP: later close/free of the leader leaves a live sibling fd whose PERF_IOC_FLAG_GROUP ioctl follows the stale group_leader into freed memory via perf_event_for_each()/perf_event_for_each_child().
flaw_origin: Original sibling-detach implementation in 8a49542c0554af7d0073aac0ee73ee65b807ef34 (perf_events: Fix races in group composition). That commit first added perf_group_detach() and the sibling branch that list_del_init's the sibling, decrements nr_siblings, and returns without setting event->group_leader = event. Parent ac9721f3f54b27a16c7e1afb2481e7ee95a70318 has no perf_group_detach; leader teardown there used perf_destroy_group(), which did reset sibling->group_leader. Later list-field renames, group_generation, and 2014 hotplug DETACH_GROUP callers reused those same lines; they did not first-write them.
